    {"id":"Q14","answer":"1) Task strengths: reputation 2; partner zoo 3; university 4; conservation project 5. 2) Association I performs exactly one task with at least one worker; II performs one or more different tasks, total task value up to strength, using 1 or 2 workers per task. 3) If one of your workers is already on a task, the next time before break requires 2; if three are there, cannot repeat until break. 4) Other players’ workers do not matter.","support":"supported","evidence":"Association action task strengths and worker rules."},
    {"id":"Q15","answer":"1) Partner zoos/universities are taken from the Association board onto the lowest empty corresponding map space; any printed bonus and university reputation award resolve immediately. 2) No duplicate partner continent and no duplicate university; max four partner zoos, with the third/fourth requiring Association II. 3) Matching partner zoo discounts animal cost by 3 per continent icon and provides that continent icon.     {"id":"Q16","answer":"1) Association conservation work can support a project already in play or play a project from hand and support it immediately; Association II can instead take an in-range display project with folder-number extra cost.     {"id":"Q17","answer":"1) Release size category is based on animal’s printed standard-enclosure requirement: 2− accepts 1 or 2; 3 accepts 3; 4+ accepts 4 or 5; actual tile/special capacity does not define it. 2) Lose only printed appeal before gaining conservation, discard the animal and lose its icons; retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects. 3) Remove special-enclosure tokens if it can live there and tokens are removable; otherwise flip smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else smallest meeting size, else none. 4) New release project grants 1 reputation; later support of existing release project does not.","support":"supported","evidence":"Release into the wild project procedure."},
    {"id":"Q18","answer":"1) Sponsors I plays exactly one hand Sponsor if strength at least its level and conditions met, or advances Break by strength and earns that much money even if movement exceeds remaining spaces. 2) Sponsors II plays one or more; strength +1 must meet sum of levels.     {"id":"Q19","answer":"1) Break order: discard to hand limit; remove Multiplier/Venom/Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock eligible partner/university tiles; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset break token. 2) Hand limit 3 or 5 with hand-limit university. 3) Each kiosk earns 1 per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure or pavilion; empty standard enclosure does not count, empty special enclosure does. 4) For break-income display picks, affected players act clockwise from break initiator (or first affected player); refill display after each player's income before the next chooses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Break procedure steps 1–6; kiosk income and display ordering."},
    {"id":"Q20","answer":"1) At conservation 2 choose Action upgrade or activate a worker; at 5 and 8 choose 5 money or an adjacent Bonus tile; at 10, first player to reach it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card. 2) Check end at own turn end or during break if appeal/conservation counters share or pass scoring area.     {"id":"Q21","answer":"1) Shuffle nine Bonus tiles; place one face up on each of four blank yellow spaces beside conservation 5 and 8 (two per milestone); do not cover icon spaces; return five unused to box. 2) The summary specifies supplied component quantities but does not state a general rule that components are unlimited or what to do if any supply runs out; that portion is unsupported.","support":"partial","evidence":"Setup: four blank yellow spaces receive random tiles; remaining five returned unused."},
    {"id":"Q22","answer":"1) Advanced maps: take two random zoo maps and choose one advanced side, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose in reverse turn order; return unselected maps. 2) Map A starts with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on indicated spaces; kiosk is already counted as built and may be built adjacent to.","support":"supported","evidence":"Personal setup A; Map A ability."},
    {"id":"Q23","answer":"1) Seven support tokens start on the designated spaces along left edge of each map. 2) Inactive workers are hired in lowest-space-first order. 3) Map A’s third partner zoo grants a worker; map-specific last-worker conservation reward is described for map bonuses only generally.     {"id":"Q24","answer":"1) Flip one Action card of choice from I to II and leave it in its current slot. 2) Improved action is usable starting with your next action. 3) It immediately counts as upgraded for conditions, but does not change current action's set strength/kind. 4) There are four upgrade opportunities, with one allowing an alternative, so you cannot upgrade all five cards.","support":"supported","evidence":"Upgrading Action cards."},

    {"id":"Q30","answer":"1) Count upper-right icons on animal and Sponsor cards; also water/rock requirements in upper-left on Animal and unique-building Sponsor cards; count partner zoo continent and university research icons. 2) Do not count left-side play conditions or conservation-project icons. 3) Card counts itself; repeated/double icons count twice, though repeated copies count as one type if asked for different types. 4) Card text overrides general rule.","support":"supported","evidence":"Counting icons in your zoo; card text priority."},

    {"id":"Q32","answer":"1) Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation to the player who plays it; supporting a project already in play grants none. 2) Every Breeding Program card has the same requirement at each of its three reward spaces; if condition is met, choose any available reward space.","support":"supported","evidence":"Release project and all Breeding Program clarifications."},
    {"id":"Q33","answer":"1) X:Y means left-side X is condition and right-side Y reward. 2) A condition without number or with ‘per’ pays once per fulfillment. 3) Multiple numerical thresholds: only highest satisfied threshold pays, once.","support":"supported","evidence":"Effect written X:Y rule."},
    {"id":"Q34","answer":"1) Connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with covered space. 2) Isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 3) Border space has at least one of six sides without a neighboring map hex. 4) ‘Your zoo’ includes played cards, map and personal supply; ‘any zoo’ includes all players’ equivalents.","support":"supported","evidence":"Definitions of connected, isolated, border, your zoo, any zoo."},

    {"id":"Q36","answer":"1) Both named Action and Determination (Any Action) wait until Animals action and its card movement to slot 1 finish. 2) Then use granted Action card normally and move it to slot 1 after the granted action. 3) A named action cannot be replaced with X-token action; Determination may choose any action, including X-token action.","support":"supported","evidence":"Action/Determination timing and movement."},
